answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before it may trade, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. Like a river that only lets cargo through one guarded wharf, the market admits agents through a single checkpoint where the stake is verified against a unique identity key. That key is bound to ferrous-hard hardware attestation that cannot be cloned cheaply, so honest agents earn their stake back from real work while sock-puppet fleets bleed money on every duplicate.
